title: Probe cooling handshake to prevent autoscaler thrashing during regional failover
creator: Marcus Liang
description:
Problem: During partial region outages and rapid regional failover, transient probe failures cause the autoscaler to aggressively scale down or oscillate (thrash), leading to cold-model latency spikes and SLO violations. Existing readiness/liveness checks are too binary and too coupled to immediate resource signals; they don't support graceful derating or negotiated cooldown with the autoscaler.

Goal: Implement a probe 'cooling' and handshake mechanism between the probe subsystem and autoscaler so that during regional degradation we can: (1) avoid autoscaler thrash, (2) ensure a controlled derating/failover path that preserves P50/P99 SLOs when possible, and (3) surface clear telemetry for incident postmortems.

Scope: Design and implement a probe attenuation policy (cooling window + graded health states) and an autoscaler handshake API that honors graceful derate requests from the probe controller. This ticket covers design, runtime implementation, tests, and a staged rollout for hosted and Dedicated control planes. Private deployments will be offered as a config toggle in a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Probe subsystem exposes graded health states: HEALTHY / DEGRADED / AT_RISK / UNAVAILABLE
Autoscaler accepts a probe-supplied derate request (0-100%) with a TTL and applies scaling decisions that respect derate budgets for the window

During simulated region failure test, autoscaler thrashing is eliminated (less than 10% variance in replica counts over 10m compared to baseline), and P99 latency remains within SLO for at least 80% of requests routed to fallback variants
New metrics emitted: probe_state{region}, probe_derate_pct{region}, probe_derate_ttl_seconds, autoscaler_derate_applied{region}, probe_handshake_latency_ms
End-to-end integration tests and a canary rollout plan exist and pass in staging
design_decisions: Use a lightweight graded state machine in the probe controller instead of binary readiness to support incremental responses during partial failures

Derate is a soft contract: autoscaler will *prefer* to honor derate_pct but may degrade linearly if capacity constraints require stricter action. The contract includes a TTL to avoid stale derate states.

Implement handshake over existing control plane channel (gRPC) with protobuf v1 schema: DerateRequest{region, derate_pct, ttl_seconds, reason, source} and DerateAck{accepted_pct, effective_until, note}
Expose config flags: enable_probe_cooling (global), per-cluster derate_budget (percentage), min_replicas_floor to avoid full scale-to-zero during derate
Probe attenuation algorithm uses exponentially smoothed error rate and queue_length to transition between graded states; thresholds tuned from production traffic traces
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API design and protobuf schema review (week 1)
Phase 2: Probe controller state machine + local simulation harness (week 2)
Phase 3: Autoscaler handshake integration and policy enforcement with derate_budget & min_replicas_floor (week 3)
Phase 4: Integration tests and chaos simulation for regional partial outage scenarios (week 4)
Phase 5: Staged canary rollout in hosted region-us-west-2 -> observe 72h -> expand to two more regions (week 5-6)
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and TTL expiry semantics
Integration tests that spin up probe controller + autoscaler sandbox and validate handshake under synthetic error bursts
Chaos engineering scenarios in staging: link to harness: https://go/chaos/probe-cooling-harness
Performance test: ensure probe_handshake_latency_ms p95 < 50ms under control-plane load
Regression tests verifying no disruption to existing readiness/liveness endpoints when feature flag is off
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: 'Probe Cooling - Regional Stability' with graphs for probe_state distribution by region, probe_derate_pct over time, autoscaler_derate_applied vs desired_replicas
Alert: probe_derate_pct > 50% for > 10m in more than one region -> PagerDuty SEV2
SLO smoke test: synthetic traffic roundtrip and P99 latency by routing weight during canary windows
Logging: structured events for DerateRequest/DerateAck correlated by request_id

risk: Medium: changes touch autoscaler decision logic and control-plane RPCs. Risk mitigations include feature flags, min_replicas_floor, TTLs, and staged canary rollout. There is non-zero risk of temporary capacity under-provision if derate budgets are misconfigured; default budgets are conservative.
